name: Skills For Real Engineers (Matt Pocock)
what: A set of small, composable agent skills for everyday engineering work with Claude Code, Codex and other agents, from Matt Pocock. They target common failure modes: grill-me and grill-with-docs have the agent ask you detailed questions before it starts (the docs version also builds a shared glossary for your project and records decisions), tdd pushes a write-a-failing-test-first loop, diagnosing-bugs runs a step-by-step debugging process, to-spec turns a discussion into a spec, and improve-codebase-architecture surveys a codebase for structural improvements. The skills are meant to be adapted and work with any model. MIT licensed.
who: Developers who already use a coding agent on real projects and want lightweight, editable workflows for planning, testing and debugging rather than a framework that takes over the whole process.

setup.code:
codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills
codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock

setup.text: Cursor, OpenCode, Windsurf and other agents (copies editable skill files into your project; update later with npx skills@latest update):

Pick one install method per agent; installing both the plugin and the copied files gives you every skill twice. Then run the setup-matt-pocock-skills skill once in each repo: it asks which issue tracker you use, which triage labels you apply and where to save docs.

prompts: Grill me about this feature before you write any code.
Use the tdd skill to add input validation to the signup form.
Use diagnosing-bugs to find out why the checkout total is off by one cent.
